# cato_role (Resource)

Manages an account-owned custom RBAC role. Updates replace the complete permission set. Import using ACCOUNT_ID:ROLE_ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cato_role" "viewer" {
  name = "Terraform site viewer"
  # description = "Read access to sites"
  permissions = [{ resource = "Sites", action = "VIEW" }]
  # account_id = "123456" # Defaults to the provider account.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Custom role name.
- `permissions` (Attributes Set) Complete permission set. Each resource occurs once; [] grants no permissions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))

### Optional

- `account_id` (String) Owning account; defaults to the provider account. Changes require replacement.
- `description` (String) Role description. Removing it clears the remote description.

### Read-Only

- `applicable_account_type` (Set of String) Destination account types on which the role can be applied.
- `id` (String) Terraform identifier in ACCOUNT_ID:ROLE_ID format.
- `is_used_on_external_access` (Boolean) Whether external access currently uses this role.
- `predefined` (Boolean) Whether this role is predefined. Predefined roles cannot be managed.
- `role_id` (String) API role identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Required:

- `action` (String) Granted action: VIEW or EDIT.
- `resource` (String) Resource identifier from cato_permission_catalog.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cato_role.viewer ACCOUNT_ID:ROLE_ID
```
